title: Role boundary enforced at the controller layer with full action audit

scope_out: must not move the authorization check below the controller layer; must not allow a user to hold more than one role; must not update or delete an existing audit_event row

entities.name: Role boundary enforced at the controller layer with full action audit

operations.text:
1. Append one `audit_event` SQLAlchemy table class to the table registry `backend/src/repository/models.py` (owned by E1-S1, existing) — the single-row shared-registry append.
2. Add `backend/migrations/versions/0002_audit_event.py` (new): creates the insert-only `audit_event` table (`id`, `actor_user_id`, `action`, `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `comment`, `reason_code`, `occurred_at`), indexed on `(entity_type, entity_id, occurred_at DESC)`, per `data-models.md`.
3. Define `AuditRepository.insert(entry: AuditEntry) -> AuditEntry` and `AuditRepository.list(entity_type=None, entity_id=None)` — insert-only, no update or delete method (D-E) — in `backend/src/repository/identity/audit_repository.py` (new), using `AuditEntry` from `backend/src/types/identity.py` (owned by E1-S1, existing).
4. Define `audit(actor, action, entity_type, entity_id, comment=None, reason_code=None) -> AuditEntry` in `backend/src/service/identity/audit.py` (new), calling `AuditRepository.insert` from step 3 — covers the AC4 audit-append behavior.
5. Define `require_roles(*roles: Role) -> Callable[..., User]` — the single enforcement point (D-F) — in `backend/src/api/authz.py` (new), built on the `get_current_user` dependency in `backend/src/api/deps.py` (owned by E1-S1, existing): raises `401` with no or invalid session before any handler body executes (AC1), and `403` when the authenticated `User.role` is not one of `roles` (AC2).
6. Define `GET /audit-entries`, guarded by `require_roles(ADMIN)` from step 5, in `backend/src/api/identity/audit_routes.py` (new), returning `AuditEntry[]` via `AuditRepository.list` from step 3.
7. Apply `require_roles(ADMIN)` from step 5 to the existing `POST /products/{product_code}/policy-versions` route, and call `audit(...)` from step 4 after a successful publish, in `backend/src/api/policy/routes.py` (owned by E1-S1, existing) — this deepens the tracer's deliberately unenforced route per D-F, which rules out any per-route hand-written check, closing the enforcement gap E1-S1's Scope Out left for this story.
8. Append one `include_router` line for `identity.audit_routes.router` to the app factory's router registry in `backend/src/api/app.py` (owned by E15-S1, existing) — the one legitimate shared-surface edit.
9. Add the schema-driven authorization suite in `backend/tests/architecture/test_route_authorization.py` (new): enumerate every UNDERWRITER/ADMIN route from `GET /openapi.json`, assert `401` with no session and no handler body execution (AC1); assert `403` for a CUSTOMER session on those routes while each role reaches its own surfaces with `200` (AC2); assert 100% of the enumerated routes are covered by both cases and that the suite fails when a new route is left unguarded (AC3); and, after an authenticated ADMIN policy-version publish, assert one `audit_event` row exists carrying the acting user id and a timestamp (AC4) — covering AC1-AC4.
